newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Poll shows 75 pct of Israelis want new government.
newsitem.headline: Poll shows 75 pct of Israelis want new government.

text.p: An opinion poll published on Monday showed nearly 75 percent of Israelis would prefer to put Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's troubled coalition out of existence.
"This is certainly a red light for the government," said Dori Shadmon, who conducted the Teleseker poll for Israel's Channel One Television.
Teleseker spokeswoman Margalit Toledano told Reuters the poll this week of 500 Israelis showed that only 22.3 percent favoured the government's continued existence as is.
Of the total, 43.9 percent supported calling early elections while 31.0 percent backed a formation of a national unity government between Netanyahu's Likud party and the opposition Labour party.
The remaining 2.8 percent had no opinion, she said. The poll had a margin of error of 4.3 percent.

Israel's peace talks with Palestinians have been plunged into crisis under Netanyahu, and his cabinet has been crumbling amid criticism of his leadership with two ministers quitting and a third threatening to follow suit.
The spokeswoman said the new poll showed that among Likud voters in national elections 13 months ago, 65 percent now say they would prefer an alternative to the government in its present makeup.

"This is in essence an indication of a dissatisfaction I believe with the performance of the present government...75 percent would prefer other options to the continuing service of the government," Shadmon told the television.
